text:
maya: Noticing a p95 latency jump in canary for /v1/generate since the 10:02 deploy. Small traffic slice but consistent. Anyone watching? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 10:02 -> 10:08: 7% traffic to v3.0.2. Telemetry: p95 latency +48% and error rate +0.8%. Autotrigger: recommend soft rollback. (reason: latency_threshold)

jon: Thanks — saw the alert. Do we have traces? Is it KV cache warm vs kernel regression?

alex: Quick check: traces show increased queue time on the sequence-length 1-64 bucket. Not obviously KV miss. Could be scheduler/kernel.

maya: If deploy-bot is recommending soft rollback, I'd prefer staged traffic back to previous variant rather than full revert. Less blast radius and keeps canary health checks intact.

ops_lead: Agreed. We should do a partial rollback to 0% for canary traffic, keep rollout paused, and pin v2.9.8 for the release window. Who can execute?

jon: I can run the staged rollback. Plan: 1) Pause canary rollout. 2) Shift canary slice 7% -> 0% (staged traffic withdraw). 3) Pin default route to v2.9.8 for this change window. 4) Update release notes & notify external ops. 5) Kick an incident investigation ticket.

maya: +1. Add a comms blurb for affected customers. We'll avoid calling it "revert" in public — use "performance stabilization".

deploy-bot: Command suggestion: `/deploy rollback --type soft --target-tag v2.9.8 --scope canary --drain-method staged --note "stabilize latency"`

jon: Running now:
```
# pause rollout
deployctl pause --rollout-id r-12345
# shift traffic
deployctl traffic-shift --rollout-id r-12345 --from v3.0.2 --to v2.9.8 --percent 7 --step 7
# pin
deployctl pin --route /v1/generate --tag v2.9.8 --reason "stabilize latency after canary spike"
```

maya: tagging SRE to watch for p95 drop once traffic shifts. @ops_lead please confirm customer comm template.

ops_lead: Using template: "We've applied a performance stabilization step in the 10:00 change window to ensure predictable latency. No action required from customers." I'll paste to #customer-comms in a minute.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused (r-12345). Traffic shift started: 7 -> 0 over 1 step. Estimated completion ~20s.

jon: Shift complete. Pin removed previous unpinned state, now pinned to v2.9.8.

maya: Telemetry update: p95 dropped ~42% back to baseline within 60s. Error rate stable. Great.

alex: Opening a follow-up ticket for a kernel/scheduler regression hypothesis: ticket #INC-7321. Assigning to eng-runtime. Include sample traces and the canary payload.

jon: Added notes to release notes draft: "10:02 deploy to v3.0.2: soft rollback to v2.9.8 performed due to elevated latency in canary; traffic reduced and default pinned during the change window. Investigation ongoing."

ops_lead: Good. I'll send to customer ops with the template and mention minimal impact. Also flag to sales for any active demos.

deploy-bot: Post-action checklist: Rollback type=soft, scope=canary, old_tag=v2.9.8, rolled_back_tag=v3.0.2, pin=true. If we need full revert, run `/deploy revert --to v2.9.8 --force`

maya: For the postmortem, capture timeline, metrics pre/post shift, and decision rationale (soft rollback chosen to reduce user-visible churn). Also note operator override step and who executed.

jon: Logged timeline and attached trace samples to #incidents and INC-7321.

alex: Suggest we add a small unit test for the scheduler path that matches canary payload pattern to catch regressions earlier.

ops_lead: Agreed. We'll schedule a quick runtime triage meeting at 13:00 today. If engineering needs a hotfix before next change window, escalate to on-call.

maya: Closing thread — canary stable, pin in place, comms sent. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: automated rollback was suppressed because human operator (jon) intervened and chose soft rollback. Audit log: action by jon at 1768888923.
